My name is Andrea Perlato. I started my scientific career at the University of Verona, School of Medicine, where I investigated the neural mechanisms underlying attention and cognitive control and earned a PhD in Neuroscience.

My research combines quantitative methods, statistics, machine learning, natural language processing, and artificial intelligence to study complex biomedical and scientific data.
My work spans neuroscience, scientometrics, knowledge representation, and ontology engineering, with a particular focus on developing semantic frameworks for organizing and analyzing large-scale scientific knowledge.
My research has also included neurodevelopmental disorders, particularly attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), integrating clinical, cognitive, and statistical approaches.

Drawing on this background, I created Inferenza to make statistical reasoning clearer and more useful for researchers working with real scientific data. The site is dedicated to applied statistics for scientific research, with a particular focus on biomedical and medical applications. Here, I explore statistical methods, the interpretation of scientific evidence, common methodological problems, and the practical use of quantitative approaches in research.

You can find more about my work on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/andreaperlato/){target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"} and [ORCID](https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0114-3567){target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"}, and visit my [YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/@andreaperlatoscience){target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"}.
